solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Architectural decoration such as flying dragon round a new church

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', that is, such as

indicators.note: something flying is scattered through the air, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church is adorned with a carving of a flying dragon wrapped around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' governs the dragon together with everything it goes round, so all of 'a new church' joins the mix; 'such as' stays outside it, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-and-anchor is a moulding of alternating egg shapes and arrow-like darts, a classic carved ornament on cornices.

clue.text: It's analogous to alcohol — tamper with can drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is all over the place, so these letters stagger into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tampering with a can of booze, which is of course a lot like alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links alcohol and 'drunk' to a tampered can of drink; the chemistry is the real subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercaptan, or thiol, is the sulphur counterpart of an alcohol, with SH in place of the OH group.

clue.text: Cross about dash of scotch in honeyed drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes all the way round the other

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: a dash is just a small splash, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of scotch

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a dash of Scotch whisky being added to a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry but is the noun for a hybrid animal; the S sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulse is an old drink of wine or water boiled and mixed with honey, so a honey-sweetened beverage.

clue.text: Milkmaid involved in opening up what used to be shed, sadly

definitions.text: what used to be shed, sadly

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top
something involved in another is caught up inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
dey is an old word for a dairymaid

explanation.surface: A milkmaid caught up in some opening ceremony is weeping over what she once had.
explanation.walkthrough: The milkmaid sits just before the last letter of the opening, and the whole is then read upwards. Shakespeare used this word for a tear, hence 'used to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is what someone weeping lets fall, and eyedrop is an archaic Shakespearean word for one.

clue.text: Weathered Ring? You'd need a good seat for that!

definitions.text: You'd need a good seat for that!

parts.note: a ship rode out, or weathered, a storm
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ringside spectator is warned to book a good seat for a weather-beaten arena show.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'good seat' in riding means a firm balance in the saddle, which bronco riders need; the joke is that spectators want a good seat too.
explanation.definitionFit: At a rodeo cowboys ride bucking broncos and bulls, which demands a secure riding posture in the saddle.

clue.text: Royal initials flanked by a kingly beast and a heraldic bird

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something flanked by another has it on both sides, so it sits inside

parts.note: the lion is king of beasts
Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A coat of arms shows the royal monogram between a lion and an eagle-like bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal initials split the beast after its first letter rather than sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An alerion is an eagle shown in heraldry without beak or feet, a stylised bird on coats of arms.

clue.text: Rate of progress one's shown at foot of page

indicators.note: in a down entry, the foot is the bottom, so this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A progress rate is reported in a footnote at the bottom of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'one is'; ACE comes beneath P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace means speed, the rate at which something moves forward or develops.

clue.text: Antique braced framework, post-Restoration in part

indicators.note: only a part of the preceding words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the hyphen, from the end of post into the start of Restoration

explanation.surface: A piece of antique furniture is said to date from after the Restoration of Charles II.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antique' is not about furniture age: it marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trest is an old form of trestle, a supporting frame of a beam on splayed, braced legs.

clue.text: A club admits balance sheet being worthless

definitions.note: a noun phrase, the state of worthlessness, where the answer is a noun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the club holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
BS is the abbreviation for balance sheet

explanation.surface: A sports club confesses that its accounts show it to be worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is the weapon, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambsace, double ace or the lowest throw at dice, figuratively means bad luck or something of no value.

clue.text: E.g. radio contact 'unmasked' mole, etc

indicators.note: unmasked suggests a disguise thrown off, so the letters appear in another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy ring's radio link exposes a mole and his associates.
explanation.definitionFit: Telecom, short for telecommunications, covers radio and telephone links: communicating over distance.

clue.text: Slide flat board round shifting scanner, patient's head involved

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the board goes about the other letters

parts.note: a tray is a flat board for carrying things

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters move into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a head is the top or front of something, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: head of patient is its first letter

explanation.surface: A patient lies on a flat board while a scanner moves round their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' puts the patient's initial in with the scanner letters before they are mixed; the board then splits as TRA...Y around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A transparency is a photographic slide, a positive image on film viewed by projected light.

clue.text: Fellow, before turning over, rises from bed

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: the thing that rises from the sea bed

parts.note: a guy is a man or fellow

indicators.note: turning over flips something, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: to means before in telling time, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: A man rolls over before getting out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the sea bed, not a sleeper's; and 'before' is the time-telling to.
explanation.definitionFit: A guyot is a flat-topped seamount, an undersea mountain that rises from the ocean floor.

clue.text: One prone to protect limb — it deflects raindrops

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: someone prone is lying down, a lier
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone lying down shields an arm to keep the rain off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' tempts towards liable, but here it means lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: A larmier is a projecting course or drip moulding on a building that throws rainwater off the wall.

clue.text: Smaller raptor in grip of eagle, dead

indicators.note: something in the grip of words is held inside them, a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run from inside eagle into dead

explanation.surface: A small bird of prey is caught by an eagle and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Glede is an old name for the kite, a bird of prey smaller than an eagle.

clue.text: Congo river: a broad segment flowing east-west

indicators.note: across entries read west to east, so flowing east to west runs the letters backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a lobe is a broad rounded section, as of a leaf or lung

explanation.surface: A geography note describing a wide stretch of a river in the Congo running westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a river's course; the direction is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebola is a river in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which gave its name to the virus.

clue.text: Journos show off about writings being circulated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to preen is to show off one's appearance

indicators.note: circulated suggests something turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts

explanation.surface: Journalists boast about their articles being widely shared.
explanation.definitionFit: Journos is slang for journalists, and pressmen are people working for the press.

clue.text: Tyrannical — and no nicer after reforming

indicators.note: reforming means reshaping, so the letters are made over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A despot who claims to have reformed turns out to be no nicer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neronic means like the Roman emperor Nero, notorious for cruelty and despotism.

clue.text: Battle almost over — discharges required

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

explanation.surface: A battle nearly over, soldiers needing to be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharges' suggests soldiers released; it means electric sparks.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcs are luminous electrical discharges that jump across a gap between electrodes.

clue.text: One of the spiraeas: doctor top row in arrangement

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into an order, here a new one for these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener tells someone to fix the top row of spiraea plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the anagram signal for top row; it is DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropwort is a meadowsweet relative, a plant of the genus Filipendula long classed with the spiraeas.

clue.text: What discerning pubs offer on everything English one's tucked into (7, two words)

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: something tucked into another goes inside it

parts.note: all means everything
a means one
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A good pub offers everything English, with a nod to the drinker who likes something traditional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's tucked into' means one is tucked into 'everything English'; 're' for 'on' is the crossword sense of 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is traditional cask-conditioned beer, prized by connoisseurs and served in good pubs.

clue.text: Set up poor rickety houses, causing head complaint

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round
to house is to give shelter, so one piece holds the other inside
rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
rig, to set up equipment, read upwards

explanation.surface: Poor-quality houses built in a hurry give their tenants headaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' does double duty: set is the word for rigging equipment, and up turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Porrigo is an old medical term for scalp diseases, such as ringworm, that affect the skin of the head.

clue.text: Artist almost touched ferny scales

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a stock abbreviation for an artist
touched means mad, mental

explanation.surface: An artist is nearly moved by ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' reads as moved but here means slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramenta are the thin brownish scales found on the stems and leaves of ferns.

clue.text: Adult chaps mature, tame no longer

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
chaps are men
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Grown men mature and are no longer docile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' reads as 'not tame any more'; it marks the answer as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenage is an obsolete verb in Spenser meaning to domesticate or tame.

clue.text: Obsessively obstinate heroine in the solarium?

parts.note: anal, from anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy and rigid
Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A stubborn, fussy heroine is found sunbathing in a tanning salon.
explanation.walkthrough: A solarium is literally a sundial, not a tanning room; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: An analemma is the figure-of-eight scale on a sundial showing the sun's declination over the year.

clue.text: Believer in polyandry out of order in Iran

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man with several husbands is considered out of order in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nairs are a Kerala caste who historically practised polyandry, a woman having several husbands.

clue.text: Cheap fags offer a price on lives

parts.note: to bid is to offer a price
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: Someone bids on lives in exchange for cheap cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a fag is a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidis are thin hand-rolled Indian cigarettes of tobacco wrapped in a leaf, sold very cheaply.

clue.text: Partner captivated by distinctive character, not a dilettante

definitions.note: the 'not a' also works as the deletion signal

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so one piece is placed inside the other
not a means one letter a is left out

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive atmosphere about someone
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A partner is taken with someone's personality and is no mere dabbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' does double duty: it removes one A from the character word and also completes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love rather than pay; a dilettante dabbles, and the two are close.

clue.text: Instruction manual? Time put in reversed major setback

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the letters run the other way
put in means inserted, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An instruction book admits that time spent on it was a big setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual' looks like a handbook in the ordinary sense; a tutor here is a teaching book for an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a book of instruction, as in a piano or guitar tutor, used for learning to play.

clue.text: Like a wild horse, old, a broken ruin, died

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
d is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An old wild horse, a broken wreck, has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' suggests a broken-in horse, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrid is an archaic form of unridden; a wild horse has never been mounted.

clue.text: Short humorous poem

parts.note: surface reading: any brief comic verse
setter's reading: this was the Azed clue-writing competition word, given only a plain definition

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle, solvers write their own clue for one entry, so it is printed with a bare definition only.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a four-line comic biographical verse, invented by Edmund Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: In Wandsworth I stay, shut up

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Wandsworth through I into stay

explanation.surface: Someone stays in Wandsworth, a district of south London, keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hist is an old interjection used to call for silence, like hush or be quiet.

clue.text: Pious Jew took refuge, when given shelter

indicators.note: something given shelter is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: hid means took refuge
as means when

explanation.surface: A devout Jew hid from persecution when someone sheltered him.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly Orthodox Jewish movement known for devotion and piety.

clue.text: Position for helmsman, sailor midway between poles

indicators.note: midway between two things is set inside them, so they flank it

parts.note: the south pole, the first of two poles
a tar is a sailor
the north pole, the second of two poles

explanation.surface: A navigator places a sailor halfway between the North and South Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poles' supplies both S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Starn is a dialect form of stern, the rear of a ship where the helmsman steers.

clue.text: Soil I got riddled, extracting old form of haematite

indicators.note: riddled means passed through a sieve, so the letters are sifted into a new order
extracting means taking out, so one letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Sifting through soil, a prospector extracts an old iron ore.
explanation.walkthrough: One O is taken from the soil letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligist is a name for crystallised haematite, the iron oxide also called specular iron ore.

clue.text: Latin? Progress being retrograde I'll attend college for science

indicators.note: to attend is to accompany, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: go means progress
I'll is I will, the I that will attend
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A student whose progress in Latin is going backwards will go to college to study science.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the science of reasoning, the formal study of valid inference.

clue.text: Apple, mostly rosy, shared billing

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a costard is a large English cooking apple
rosy means red

explanation.surface: An apple, mostly rosy, is shown on the menu alongside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' looks as if it trims rosy; it trims the apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Two actors who costarred appeared together with equal top billing in a film or play.
